transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um… honestly, work is the big reason I’m here. I’m a maintenance worker, and I’ve been having this problem where I keep forgetting things I’m supposed to follow up on—scheduled callbacks, work orders, little things I tell people I’ll check on and then I just… don’t. Or I remember way too late, after someone’s already upset or it’s become a bigger issue.

It’s not like I don’t care. That’s the part that’s been bothering me, because I do care, and I’ll fully mean it when I say, “I’ll call you back,” or “I’ll put that work order in,” or “I’ll circle back after I check that.” But then the day gets going, I get pulled into something else, and it’s just gone until somebody asks me about it again. And by then it looks like I blew them off.

It’s piled up enough now that my job basically sent me here. I’ve been trying to move up, and I feel like I’m about to ruin my chance because people are starting to see me as unreliable. That’s what scared me. I don’t want to lose my shot over forgetting basic follow-ups.
Did you have this same kind of problem with forgetting follow-through and losing track of tasks when you were a child?

Yeah… yes, I think so. I mean, looking back, it wasn’t just something that started with this job or with adult responsibilities. I remember being like this even in grade school.

Teachers would say I was smart — like, “She understands the work,” that kind of thing — but then I’d lose the paper I was supposed to turn in, or I’d only do part of what the directions said because I missed some piece of it. I’d have worksheets shoved in my desk or backpack and then not be able to find them. And I needed reminders to finish classwork, not because I couldn’t do it, but because I’d kind of drift off from what I was supposed to be completing and then the time would be gone.

So, yeah, it feels familiar. The job makes it more obvious now because there are consequences and people waiting on me, but that pattern of losing track and needing reminders… that goes way back.
Do you have the same kind of forgetting and losing track of things in your life outside of work, too?

Yeah… I mean, I guess the biggest thing is still work, because that’s where it’s getting me in real trouble. That’s what brought me in — I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and even basic follow-ups I promised people I’d do. Like I’ll tell someone, “Yeah, I’ll check on that and get back to you,” and I really do mean it in the moment, but then it just slips away.

And now it’s not just one little mistake here or there. It’s piled up enough that work actually sent me here, which is embarrassing to say. I’m trying to move up, and I feel like I’m putting that at risk because people are starting to see me as not following through.

Outside of work… I mean, I’m sure there are little examples, but the work stuff is the clearest and the most upsetting because there are people waiting on me and there are consequences. That’s where it’s become impossible to ignore.
Outside of work, do these same problems with forgetting and not following through cause trouble in your home life or relationships?

Um… I’m honestly not sure how much, if that makes sense. I don’t want to say no, because I’m sure there are things at home where I forget something or don’t follow through right away, but I also don’t have a clear example jumping out at me the way the work stuff does.

Like at work, it’s very obvious because there’s a work order, or a callback, or someone waiting, and then it reflects badly on me. At home it’s more… I don’t know, it blends into regular life more, maybe? I might forget something and then just deal with it later, or it’s not as formal, so nobody’s writing it down or getting on me about it in the same way.

In relationships, I guess I’d have to think about that more. I haven’t really had someone sit me down and say, “This is a major problem,” at least not in the way work has. So I don’t want to overstate it. The thing I know for sure is that work is where it’s causing the most trouble and where people are actually upset with me about it.
At home, do you also often forget things you said you would do?

At home… I mean, yes, I do forget things I said I’d do, but the part that’s really gotten bad enough to bring me in is more with work. That’s where it’s not just, like, “Oh, I forgot to pick something up,” and then I fix it later. It’s scheduled callbacks, work orders, and basic follow-ups I told people I would handle.

I’ll tell someone, “I’ll call you back,” or “I’ll check that work order,” or “I’ll get back to you on that,” and in the moment I fully mean it. I’m not blowing them off. But then it just… disappears from my head, or I lose track of it in everything else, and by the time I realize, it’s already late or someone else is asking why it wasn’t done.

And it’s piled up so much that work actually sent me here, which is honestly really embarrassing. I’m trying to move up, and now I feel like I could lose that chance because people are seeing me as someone who doesn’t follow through. So yes, I can forget things outside of work too, but the clearest, most serious version of it is these work things I promised I’d do and then didn’t keep track of.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

I don’t know… I mean, I worry about the work situation because it’s become a real problem, but I’m not sure if I’d say I’m anxious or worried “often” in the way you mean.

Like, if something is going wrong or I know I dropped the ball, then yeah, I’ll think about it and feel stressed about it. But I don’t know if I’m walking around anxious all the time, if that’s what you’re asking. I guess I’d need you to clarify a little what you mean by anxious — like nervous for no reason, or just worried because there are actual consequences happening?
In social situations with friends or family, do you also tend to lose track of conversations or forget plans you made?

With friends or family… I’m not sure I can give you as clean an answer there. I probably do sometimes, but the place I really notice that “losing the thread” thing is when my supervisor is talking directly to me.

Like, he’ll be standing right there explaining something about a repair or an audit, and I’m looking at him. I’m not looking away, I’m not trying to be rude, I’m not ignoring him. I’ll even feel like I’m listening. But then only the first part really sticks, and after that it’s like the rest doesn’t fully land. Then I have to ask him to say it again, and I hate doing that because it makes me look like I wasn’t paying attention.

So in social situations, I don’t have a strong example of forgetting plans with friends or family right now. But conversations where someone is giving me information straight to my face — yes, that happens, especially at work with my supervisor.
In your day-to-day life outside of work, do you often have trouble staying focused when someone is talking to you?

Outside of work, I’m trying to think… I don’t have as clear of an example. I’m sure there are times someone at home is talking and I’m not taking it all in, but the situation I can really point to is at work, when my supervisor is talking straight to me.

Like he’ll be explaining something about a repair or an audit, and I’m standing there looking right at him. I’m not on my phone, I’m not turned away, I’m not trying to ignore him. In my head I feel like I’m listening. But then what happens is the first part sticks, and after that it’s like the rest just doesn’t settle in. Then I’m left realizing I didn’t actually hold onto what he said, so I have to ask him to repeat it.

That’s the part that bothers me, because from the outside it probably looks like I just wasn’t paying attention, but I really am trying to listen. It’s more like I lose the thread even while he’s talking directly to me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed مؤخراً?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I wouldn’t immediately say I’ve been depressed, exactly. I mean, I’ve been stressed and frustrated, especially when things aren’t going well, but I don’t know if that’s the same as feeling “down or depressed.”

Like, if I mess something up or I feel like I’m not keeping up, then yeah, I can feel pretty bad about myself for a while. But I don’t know that I’ve been walking around feeling sad all the time, if that’s what you mean. I guess I’d need to know what you’re counting as depressed — like feeling hopeless and low most days, or just being worn out and upset because life has been difficult lately.
When someone at home is talking to you, do you often realize afterward that you missed part of what they said?

At home… I’m trying to think of a clear example, and I don’t want to just say yes if I’m not sure. I probably do miss things sometimes, but the one that really stands out to me is still at work.

When my supervisor is talking straight to me about a repair or an audit, I’ll be looking right at him like I’m following along. I’m not trying to tune him out or anything. But then only the first part really sticks, and after that it’s like the rest kind of slips past me. Then I realize I didn’t actually get all of what he said, and I have to ask him to say it again.

So with someone at home, I can’t give you a strong “this happens all the time” answer. But that same kind of thing definitely happens when someone is explaining something directly to me, especially my supervisor.
Aside from work, do you often have the same trouble staying focused or following through in other parts of your life?

Yeah, I think so. Not always in a big dramatic way, but it happens enough that I notice it.

A good example is when I’m trying to read a digital work order. I’ll open it up thinking, okay, I’ve got this, I just need to read the notes and see what they’re asking for. And I’ll start reading, but halfway through, my mind kind of slips off. Like if there’s another noise nearby, or I’m already thinking about the next job I need to get to, suddenly I realize my eyes were on the words but I don’t actually know what I just read.

Then I have to go back and reread the same part, sometimes more than once, just to figure out what the notes actually said. It’s frustrating because I’m not avoiding it, and it’s not that I don’t care. I start out focused, but it doesn’t stay there. My attention just kind of gets pulled off track before I’ve finished.
Do you often feel restless or like you have trouble sitting still?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think of myself as someone who’s constantly bouncing around or unable to sit in a chair, if that’s what you mean.

I mean, I probably shift around some, like crossing and uncrossing my legs or adjusting how I’m sitting, but I don’t know if that’s more than normal. If I’m waiting somewhere or I’m in a long conversation, I might get uncomfortable or kind of want to be done, but I wouldn’t say I’ve really noticed this as a major problem.

So… I guess my answer is I’m not sure. Trouble focusing, yes, I notice that more clearly. But feeling physically restless or like I can’t sit still — I don’t have a strong example of that.
Do you have the same trouble paying attention when you’re not at work?

Yeah, I do, although the clearest example I keep thinking of is still tied to work stuff, if that makes sense. It’s not only when someone is standing over me or when there’s pressure. Even just sitting there trying to read something on the screen, I can lose it.

Like with a digital work order, I’ll open it and think, okay, I’m going to read the notes, see what needs to be done, and then go handle it. And at first I am reading it. But halfway through, my mind just kind of slides off somewhere else. It might be because there’s another sound nearby, or I start thinking about the next job I have to get to, and then I realize I was looking right at the words but I don’t actually know what I just read.

Then I have to back up and read the same part again, sometimes more than once. It’s not that I’m trying to ignore it or that I don’t care about it. I start out thinking I’m paying attention, but it doesn’t stay locked in. It’s like my attention gets pulled away before I’ve finished taking in what I’m supposed to be reading.
When you’re not at work, do you also have trouble paying attention?

Yeah… I mean, I know I keep coming back to this example, but it’s the one that really shows what happens for me. I can sit down with something I need to read, like a digital work order, and at the start I’m thinking, okay, I’ve got this, I’m reading the notes, I’m going to understand what they want and then do it.

But then halfway through, it’s like my attention just slips off without me noticing right away. There might be a noise nearby, or I’ll start thinking about the next job I’m supposed to get to, and then I realize my eyes were still moving over the words but I don’t actually know what I just looked at.

So then I have to go back and read it again, sometimes the same part more than once. It’s not that I’m trying not to pay attention. I really do start out focused. It just doesn’t hold.
When you're at home, do you also find yourself rereading things because your mind drifts off?

Yeah, it’s kind of the same thing. At home, if I’m reading something on my phone or trying to go through instructions or a message, I can start out thinking I’m reading it, like I’m paying attention, but then partway through my mind just… slips somewhere else.

It’s similar to what happens with the digital work orders. I’ll open it and think, okay, read the notes, figure out what needs to be done, and then move on. And I’ll be looking right at the words, but then there’s a noise or I start thinking about the next thing I need to do, and suddenly I realize I don’t actually know what I just looked at. Like my eyes kept going but my brain didn’t stay with it.

So then I have to go back and reread it, sometimes more than once, which is frustrating because I’m not trying to rush or ignore it. I really do start off thinking I’ve got it, and then halfway through it’s just gone.
When something is really interesting to you, do you still have the same trouble paying attention?

Yeah… even when it’s something I’m interested in, I can still lose it if I’m trying to read through something. It’s not like interest just fixes it.

Like, I might start a digital work order and feel like, okay, I’ve got this, I’m following the notes, I understand what I’m supposed to do. And then somewhere halfway through, without really deciding to, my mind just kind of slips off. A noise will catch me, or I’ll start thinking ahead to the next job, and then I realize I’ve been looking right at the words but I don’t actually know what I just read.

That’s the part that gets me, because I’m not sitting there bored on purpose or ignoring it. I can really be trying. I can even care about getting it right. But my attention just doesn’t stay with the page or the screen the whole way through, and then I have to go back and read it again.
Do you often have trouble keeping your things organized?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, honestly. I mean, I have places where I put things, or at least I think I do, but I don’t know if I’d call it “organized” in the way other people mean it.

Like, are you asking if I have piles of stuff, or if I can’t find things, or if my tools and papers aren’t in order? Because some of that probably depends on the day and what’s going on. I wouldn’t say I’ve really sat down and thought, “Oh, this is an organization problem,” but I guess I’d need to know more what you mean by it.
Do you often have trouble finding things you need because you put them down and then can’t remember where they are?

Yes. That one, yeah… that happens a lot. More than I like to admit, honestly.

I’ll put something down for what feels like two seconds — my keys, the tablet at work, a flashlight, or a tool I was literally just using — and then it’s like it disappears. I’ll be standing there thinking, okay, I just had this in my hand, I walked over here, I set it down somewhere, and then I can’t picture where. So then I’m retracing every step, checking the same bench or cart or shelf more than once, looking under papers, looking in places that don’t even make sense.

At work it’s embarrassing because it can actually hold things up. Like if I need the tablet to check something or I need the one tool I just had, the job kind of stops while I’m hunting around for it. And I know how it looks — like I’m being careless or not keeping track of my stuff — but in the moment I really did not mean to lose it. I just set it down and my brain didn’t… record where it went, I guess.

It’s especially frustrating when it’s something obvious, like the flashlight is sitting right on a ledge or the keys are in a pocket I already checked, and I’ve spent all this time getting irritated and feeling stupid over it. It’s constant enough that I kind of expect it now, but it still slows me down.
At home, do these attention and forgetting problems cause real problems for you?

At home… yes, it causes problems, but honestly the part that’s really weighing on me right now is work. That’s where it’s turned into something serious.

It’s not just me misplacing something and getting annoyed for a few minutes. I’ve got a backlog now, and there have been tenant complaints because things aren’t getting handled as smoothly or as fast as they should. And there’s a safety review on my record, which really scares me, because that feels official, like it’s not just “oh, she’s a little scattered.” It’s documented now.

I’ve been working toward moving up, trying to get on that promotion path, and now I’m scared this is going to cost me that. Like all the years of trying to prove I can handle more responsibility could get wiped out because I can’t keep up the way I need to. It’s embarrassing, and it makes me feel like I’m constantly trying to catch up before someone notices even more.
Did these attention and forgetting problems get noticeably worse after a stressful event or period in your life?

Yes… I mean, not one single stressful event like a death or something, but there was definitely a period where it got noticeably worse.

It’s been about 11 months now, I’d say, since the new management company came in and changed our department over to digital work orders and much stricter documentation. That’s when I really started noticing that the attention and forgetting stuff wasn’t just annoying — it was affecting my actual work in a bigger way.

Before that, I had my own ways of keeping track of things, even if they probably looked messy to somebody else. But once everything had to be entered digitally and documented more tightly, with all these steps that have to be followed, it felt like there was a lot more to hold in my head and a lot more chances for me to miss something or lose track of where I was. And since then it’s just been… harder. Like the same problems were there, but the new system made them stand out a lot more, and I haven’t really caught up.

Before that, I had my own ways of keeping track of things, even if they probably looked messy to somebody else. But once everything had to be entered digitally and documented more tightly, with all these steps that have to be followed, it felt like there was a lot more to hold in my head and a lot more chances for me to miss something or lose track of where I was. And since then it’s just been… harder. Like the same problems were there, but the new system made them stand out a lot more, and I haven’t really caught up.
